I dont know if its been discovered yet.. but I found something out in Debug Mode which could be a couple hours of fun if you're a sucker for Ragdoll Physics.
In Debug mode, with Caps Lock on, you can press the Spacebar to make N's body act like it was just killed : Yielding different death animations.
Also - if you hold down CTRL while in debug mode (with N dead), he will slingshot to wherever your mouse cursor is. You can slam him into walls, onto mines, and live-out those great death-falls you've always wanted to see. No matter where N is, he'll return to you, going through walls (and even through the Level Boundary, if he got thrown out there). When he combusts/explodes, however, you'll only get one of the body parts (I'm guessing his head).
Does this work for anyone else? I hope so.

~Moshpit

#158392 98 2006-03-27T04:09:51Z Mosh
Click the names of buildings on that map-thing to move to different buildings. Click "Enter *Building Name*" to enter that building if it hasn't been barricaded to a point of no-entry. Click the 'Search' button to look through the building to try to find something. When on the same 'building' (Outside or inside, either.), and you see someone under the drop-down menu next to 'Attack', named 'zombie', thats a Zombie, and you should repeateadly click the 'Attack' button (after choosing a weapon from a subsequent drop-down menu) until they die, OR, until you're around 15 AP. Once around 15 AP, go find a building with some form of Barricade (Moderately Barricaded or heavily barricaded would be good. Also - in an area with very few zombies.) and click 'Log Out'. You recieve 1AP (Action Point) every half-hour. So, 24 hours from when you last played, you'll be good-to-go.
Also - if you have no clue what to do, I'd start with the 'Firefighter' class, since its weapon (Fireaxe) required no ammo, and has a good hit-percentage. Just dont get two(or more) of your characters close to eachother on the map, or they'll be deleted automatically by the system (or suffer combat/AP penalties).
Also! If you die, and you wake up as a Zombie, make your way to a church in the right-side of a Northern District called Yagton (or something like that.). The people there are mainly medics, and will Revive you if they have the syringes. They're great guys.
Oh - join the Metanet Malitia,

Alright. I'm assuming you all know what a Doppler Sound Effect is? When you're standing somewhere, you hear a car approaching, and as the car gets closer it gets louder. Then when its going away from you, it gets quieter. Thats basically what I'm talking about.
I'm suggesting all things that are active have a Doppler Sound Effect to them. A Rocket would get louder based on how close it gets to N. The closer a Gauss is to you when it shoots, the louder it gets. Each drone would have its own individual 'mechanical' whirr, hum, or buzz - which would get louder the closer it got to you. A Floor-Guard wouldn't have a static Doppler-Effect, but if you jump over one that is scooting under you, you'll hear its sound effect for movement.
Of course, mines wouldnt have a doppler Effect (Unless chain-reactions are implemented in the next version - though I'm not suggesting this), and neither would Gold.
What do you guys think?

I put alot of thought into this after seeing gold delay used in race maps and DDA's.

Lets say you're making a map. You're stacking tons of things ontop of eachother. (switches under gold. Gold delay in DDA's. Etcetera.) What if you want an entire spot deleted, without having to click thirty times? (Such as the 20+ pieces of gold atop multiple jumpads in some DDA's)
I suggest a key+mouse-click combination (holding A and clicking in edit mode, perhaps?) that will delete all objects under the mouse in one click. Everyone might not find this useful, though A is ALOT closer to the ASWQ used in Block-Placement mode than Delete is. If people werent using it to delete stacks of items, they could just use the 'delete all' button/mouse combo and delete like normal (because they arent stacking), and then quickly shift between Block Edit Mode and Object Edit Mode.

#15442 1 2007-05-30T05:39:23Z Mosh
Launchpads that face a horizontal angle (left and right, respectively) don't do much for N's running speed. Sure, they offer a momentary boost, but only so much. Not really enough to help N scale a wall, even if placed a single tile from the sloped-corner of the wall.

Solution?

Why not add a run-speed object? I'm assuming it would have the same placement-flexibility as a Launchpad, but instead of causing a fixed velocity boost that restarts at Velocity-Zero, why not simply multiply the velocity of the Ninja? It would allow seamless speed boost in all directions, and offer an alternative - not a replacement - for the Launchpad.

Action levels would easily take advantage of the quick-response and "Guarenteed Boost" capability of launchpads, and race levels would most likely take advantage of the "Fast moving gets even faster" capability of the Velocity-Boosters.

Possibly, even, they'd have multiple different types of Velocity-Multipliers. A stripe on the object image, a color change - whatever could be used to identify the amount of velocity multiplication - whatever it would be, it would add insurmountable diversity, in a very positive way, to the gameplay. Possibly x1.5, x2, x2.5, and x5 Velocity boosters could be implemented.

They wouldn't be direction-specific, either. Simple pass through one and your velocity is increased. Maybe take a half-second graduated curve in the increase of velocity, so it isn't a sudden jerk in speed, and there you have it. Increased velocity based on current velocity.

What do you think?

Cheers,
~Mosh

Alright, here's two ideas that incorporate mirrors into N. And no, Realtime reflections of the Ninja is not one of them.

Mirror Tile
It simply has a thin colored strip on the last pixle of it's image to distinguish it as a Mirror tile. When a laser drone fires upon it, the laser bounces off, and follows through to a random coordinate - retaining normal laser principals and rules. Floorguards can travel on it normally.

Mirror Drone
A drone, with an undecided fictional speed, which has normal drone principals applied to it. When a laser hits it, lasers are emitted from all apothems (basically, the flat sides) of the drone. The original laser hits the drone and lasts normally, as if the drone was a solid object - but the Mirror Drone stops in place, taking in all of the laser energy from the original beam before firing, creating a sort of delay between Laser->Mirror, Mirror->Apothem Rays.

What do you think?

Cheers,
~Mosh

How does sending the laser back to the mirror behind it fix the problem? The laser doesn't collide with the drone. Either way, I don't like the suggestion.
Collide with the drone? Since when is the drone involved?

I proposed to treat the Mirror Object like any other object that can be "hit" by a laser - An Activated Trapdoor, a Locked Key-Door, and a closed Normal Door.

I simply said that a code for having the Laser Drone "check" if it's firing on a normal Obstruction (tile, or the three door options), or a Mirro Obstruction. If it were the Mirror Obstruction, it would reflect a laser (or create a new laser with it's source as the point of contact between Laser1 and the Mirror -) point in the direction of a corresponding angle.

It's extremely easy to do, even in N 1.4's AS build.

=Analysis=

And yes, it does work. Collisions are detencted because of a solid obstruction between the laser drone and which is triggered by N traversing into the firing view of the Laser Drone, correct? The Laser Drone, once it has "seen" N, searches for that solid, and draws the Beam. The beam is fired, and is represented as a 2-Pixle (Give or take one Pixle) beam that stretches from the center of the drone to the obstruction. A number of objects are labeled as "solid" - such as Trapdoors that are deployed, Locked Doors that have yet to be unlocked, and Normal Doors that haven't yet been opened by N's general proximity to the door. By simply adding this "solid" property to the Mirror Tile, and setting it's placement rotation to that of a Launchpad, then placement and fuctionality have come full-circle. As for the interference of "placement" and other Drones and their paths, another simple check would be used. It would seek an obstruction in front of the drone, as all drone paths do when deciding when to "turn", but the Mirror object would prevent the traveling of the drone if it were inside the square at all. It would take up more room than a standard tile if placed between two tiles (or even a Half-Tile for that matter), but it would be very simple to code as, once again, it would retain "solid" properties such as the Door Examples.

The laser searches for a collision (with a tile, or closed door, or deployed trapdoor, or locked normal door) on a line between it and the ninja until it finds one, then it draws the laser. What I'm trying to say is that the laser will detect a collisoin with the mirror, and reflect until it hits another mirror and reflect until it hits another mirror, and so on for infinity. The laser goes through both N and the drone, so if you make a room made of only mirror tiles, the laster will keep reflecting for ever and ever and never collide with anything that will make it stop, therefore the loop will continue iterating and will not alow anything else to happen because it will never finish. Since computer is stuck in a loop, that program will never get to the stage where it checks for user input (I'm assuming flash works this way; either way, it doesn't work) and since the program cannot detect user input when the user does something, Windows considers the program non-responsive (which it is) and it crashes.

Spoiler: [bWho Are The Characters?[/b]]
Spoiler: BLACKThe ninja that sees most things as we do. He can be witty, and he can also be brutally cold. He's often the most violent ninja.
Spoiler: GREENWe're not sure if she's witty or just plain dumb, Green Ninja often calls everyone "Jim". Maybe it had something to do with her ex?
Spoiler: DARK BLUEDark Blue Ninja is the oldest of all the ninjas. He's a Chef, and makes excellent Pasta (Ep.1). He also hates MTI as much as we do (Ep.9). He is also confused (or rather, ridiculed) about his sexuality; or at least his security of such (Ep's.28 and 29). Some suspect his real name to be "Dave".
Spoiler: REDRed Ninja is the "boss" ninja. He's got his head up his rump most of the time, and loves to crack jokes at other ninjas. He's a meanie. Red Ninja is also a little slow on the uptake of conversation. He's also money-hungry (Ep.15), and he gets bored on the weekends (Ep.17). Red also smokes (Ep.27).
Spoiler: TEALThe Lackey Ninja, as his boss Red Ninja calls him. He's friends with Violet Ninja, a fellow pencil-pusher under the employment of Red.
Spoiler: PURPLEHe's the inquisitor of the ninjas. He ponders a lot, and thinks things through WAY too much. He is obsessed with his hair (who would have thunk' it?), and often dyes it. This is why he appears in multiple shades of purple.
Spoiler: BROWNThe general smart-ass of the ninjas, Brown Ninja is in constant competition with his ex, Green Ninja. He hasn't been the same since Green spotted some gold lying around after he completed a level (Ep.6).
Spoiler: LIGHT BLUELight Blue, of "Lieutenant Blue" as his friends call him, is a constant storyteller. She's always mucking about how strong she is, thusly the nickname, "Lt.Blue".
Spoiler: FUTUREFuture Ninja appeared once (Ep.12), and was never seen again. I guess the whole crotch-kicking incident warded him off.
Spoiler: SANDThe only time we've ever seen a sand-colored Ninja around here is when one corrected Green by proclaiming that their name was not "Jim". Instead, they proclaimed their name to be "Animator".
Spoiler: ANTSBelieve it or not, small bugs have began training in the art of the Ninjitsu. They also seem to have an obsession with gold (Ep.23).
Spoiler: OrangeOrange Ninja has an ego problem. Simply put, he likes things to be BIG. I wonder what he's hiding...? (Ep.25)
Spoiler: BROWN-ISHThe joker of the Ninjas, Brown Ninja simply likes talking. People try to shut up his nonsense whenever possible by telling her jokes, as her laugh is slightly less annoying.
Spoiler: GOLDGold Ninja, the God of all Ninjas, makes few appearances (Ep.26). He is, of course, the creator of Gold.
Spoiler: ZAPPYThe floorguard pet of Black Ninja. Zappy enjoys playing fetch, and plotting the death of all other Ninjas.
Spoiler: DRONETICUS III, SR.While his name is never actually revealed, Droneticus, or "Droc" as he prefers to be called, nearly assassinated Black Ninja in the past (Ep.13). He likes his tea promptly at noon-thirty, and nibbles ever-so-slightly upon a scone while drinking such a brew. He's got a PhD in Neurozappologistical Application. He is also the author of three children's books.
Spoiler: LUCThe only laser drone to have allergies (Ep.24), Luc hates all things with pollen. Sadly, Gauss Turrets emit pollen after every shot.
Spoiler: KILLERKiller, or "Turtle Killer" as he is known on the street, is a notorious pet-murderer. He often disguises himself as Pink Ninja to try to give the cops the slip, and even says his murders are "accidental", by proclaiming "Oops! I stepped on -Insert Pet Here-". Be wary of him.
Spoiler: PINKPink left Red after he had called her a "Homie-G Dizzle Slice Dawg" (Ep.20). What the hell is that, anyways? Nonetheless, Pink is best friends with Green.
Spoiler: MOSHAlthough he never appears in a comic - Mosh appeared in Episode 38 - "Awake". Mosh is indeed a ninja. What color is he? Thats for him to know, and you to never find out. Mind you, he doesn't look like any conventional ninja...

Quote: kkstrong0, July 03, 2007 02:07 am
my only issue, is that the plot sometime collides with LV's antoher day

otherwise GREEEEEEEAAAAAT[/tonythetiger]
I can see where plot similarities can be seen between Sidestreet 210 and LV's Another Day. A significant difference, however, is the way the plots are presented. His plotlines, which seem to rely on the "random WOW!" factor, have a constant crew of characters which seem to operate on a satirical sense of pseudo-highbrow humor. My comics lack an instant "WOW!" factor, but achieve close to the same with very involving dialogue.

Also, look at the speech between his comic and my comic. I have a set-size of pixels I conform myself to for each strip, which is 400x700; just under a 1:2 ratio. LV's comic stretches and crops itself to meet any size requirements of the strip. This is relevant to the speech of our comics because I present much more dialogue in less of a space, while he presents less dialogue in more space. Though, what we both are doing isn't necessarily a bad thing. We both possess quite humorous comic strips, regardless of how we achieved such a title.

All-in-all, I can see similarities between the comics. I can also see, however, a vast sea of differences.

And with that being said, Episode 15 is being drawn. Paintshop Pro, here I come.

#16230 1 2007-07-14T19:57:20Z Mosh
Decipher

This game is rather simple and quite challenging at the same time.
One person, in this case being me as I'm starting the game, posts a picture of a paragraph/sentence that is written in a code, fictional language, odd position, puzzle-like placement, etc...
Also in that same image can be a few hints. These hints can also be in a code, but should be easier to decipher than the actual code if they're coded as well.

The person who deciphers the previous code gets to make their own code for the next "round" to decipher.

Also, try not to make the images gigantic in pixels.

For the sake of organization, I'll update all the code-images onto this post, and I'll also write to the right of each code round who won.

Winners
Round 1 - Spawn Of Yanni
Round 2 - Spawn Of Yanni

ROUND 3:

"Primes. I am not a bad man, I'm only one with many a thought on this sexy, interesting plan."

~Mosh

#16461 1 2007-07-30T03:00:15Z Mosh
Ever wonder if the guy next to you who is speaking very rapidly in a foreign accent is thinking in the same language as you? I mean, to some extent, it makes sense right?

Well, consider this before you jump to conclusions:
When scientists use electro-stimulation to cause the human brain to think, imagine, or remember something, it is not adjusted in any way to accommodate what language they learned first, or use most. So, on a crude and technical level, our minds use the same electric patterns to produce relatively similar thoughts, imaginations, and relatively similar images of fear.

So, if our thoughts were to be translated, what would they translate to? Would someone who grew up speaking Japanese think in a different language than someone who grew up speaking German? How do you distinguish ones language of thought, anyways? Or rather, do we all think in the same language, but just interpret it differently?

My idea of this is that we all think in the same language and do, indeed, interpret our thoughts into our native language.
What do you guys think?

#349039 17 2007-07-30T16:25:12Z Mosh
Quote: Tsukatu, July 29, 2007 08:46 pm
Unless you're willing to show me some studies in which stimulation of the very same regions produce the very same results in a wide variety of brains, it makes sense to me that different people will store their memories in different parts of any given gyrus.

This study on one individual demonstrates that even without the depicted temporal lobe of the human brain, memories can be evoked by electrode stimulation. A well-cited article, and a six-year old article at that, too. I'm surprised it hasn't been brought up more recently.
This study also shows a much more cited, well-written demonstration of electrode-stimulation through slow-oscillation (increasing and decreasing electrode stimuli above and below a certain median). While it doesn't pertain to the actual remembrance of memories, it does pertain to boosted memory on a trial-tested basis.

Also stated in the second article is a very valuable piece of information regarding the citing of past studies. It simply says they weren't very well documented in the past, and were near-random in their application. Inconvenient to anyone writing a neurostimulation thesis, but just a simple speed-bump for our discussion.

By looking at these two articles, you can come to a number of assumptions. Two of the most prominent are:
-That there is a relation between electrode stimulation of the cortical regions and memories.
or
-That there is a relation between electrode stimulation of the cortical regions and the brain thinking that it remembers something.

I also stumbled upon an article in which a similar experiment was performed on cats, but I felt it irrelevant to cite.

But even people who try to commit suicide and survive sometimes say that it is the scariest moments of their lives and that they never want to do it again, while others are sitting around waiting to get out of the hospital so they can recover and try again later. How easy is it to find these triggers when we can compare two or more people in the same situation and show the specific reason why one is suicidal and the other isn't?

anyway, that is off topic. I was just putting the idea that maybe we interpret sensory input in a language that is unique to each of us. Maybe we just find similar languages close to our own and this is how people become best friends or worst enemies.

The comparison Personal and General psychoanalysis and electrode stimulation of various cortical regions of the human mind are like comparing apples and shoelaces. True, at their very core, they might have a single particle of relevance, but other than that, they're nothing more than an assumption or an opinion.

Back to theoretical neurology - Sensory input is indeed unique to the individual. Our eyes see differently, age differently, and act differently. We smell different things. We taste things and relate them to a good or a bad taste (actually, we sense acidity of an object, but that's a different subject altogether). At it's core, sensory translation operates in a very similar, if not identical fashion to each other. The translation of sensory input (post-translated sensory acquisition) is intriguing, and may relate to Dave's theory of syntactic labeling of experience anamnesis.

#16773 1 2007-08-16T23:03:41Z Mosh
I suggest separate ratings bars for different aspects of maps, instead of one big one for the entire map. I used one of my own maps (and used real ratings and comments I received to produce such statistics) to show how it would be displayed graphically:



It would split the map into five categories: "Action", "Difficulty", "Originality", "Flow", and "Intensity".
A little overwhelming? Nope. Anyone who plays any map would easily be able to sum up the map from those categories. The ratings would also be attached to the "Post a New Comment" box, so you could only rate if you posted a comment. The comment would display a letter and a percentage for each category at the end of the post (A,D,O,F,I - respectively). Instead of the 1, 1.5, 2 - etc rating system, there would be a three-part drop-down menu to select your percentage for each category. The first box would be the 10's column (up to 9), the second would be the single-digit column (up to 9), and the decimal menu would also stretch to 9. Any vote of 99.9 would be translated as being "100%" in that category.

Also, all of the votes would be summed up in an "Overall" rating, which users can not directly pick, to give an overall display of the map's ratings. This overall rating would now actually mean something, since it is derived from unique aspects of the map and a players rating on those aspects.

This entire system (which would be easy to fabricate, using the old rating system as a model) would give actual meaning to votes, as they deal with unique parts of the map, not just the map itself.

It is also notable that the "Add To Favorites" box has moved. I think it looks great under the thumbnail, and is easier to spot. This is entirely not the focus of the suggestion, though.

Note: This would only apply to playable maps.


Simplified Version
Add five rating panels, each with one aspect of the map receiving a rating. These five are automatically combined to present an "Overall" rating. This adds meaning to the votes in a simplified fashion.


I love the idea, and I hope it gets implemented. What do you guys think?

Cheers,
~Mosh

#17212 1 2007-09-14T06:44:58Z Mosh

-What has happened so far-
UPDATE 1: Tristan received a random death-thread note from someone named "Omasi". Craig went to start repairs on a portable electricity generator to power the motel.
UPDATE 2: (Suggested by Mechtradevil) Aryn is introduced. She tells Tristan and Craig that they need new parts for the generator to work. Craig and Tristan try to find Vadeed to help them find parts in the city, and they discover someone tried to kill Vadeed in the last 24 hours. The killer said something about a "highest bidder" before Vadeed shot him. The group leaves to find parts on a 2-hour journey.
UPDATE 3:(Suggested by Axonn) The group, Vadeed, Craig, and Tristan review the map [Map Image] and plan their route behind some boulders for safety. While behind the boulders, some random soldiers begin firing upon them. Craig and Tristan take out two of them, while Vadeed finishes off the last one. They inspect a briefcase one of the soldiers, a medic, was carrying. Nearly all the papers had a large "POST DATED - X108" stamp in the middle. The papers had bullet-holes in them from the gunfight. They continue to the first checkpoint - a Subway Station.
UPDATE 4:(Suggested by Axonn) The group enters the hardware store after narrowly evading a mercenary checkpoint. The hardware store was hit by a bomb, and most of it is in general disarray. Aside from some soaps Vadeed found, and some wires and small clamps Tristan found, nothing was of use here. The group did not find the mounting brackets they had hoped to locate.
UPDATE 5:(Suggested by Mechtradevil) The group is shot at by a sniper on their way back, not more than 500 meters from the doors of the hardware store. Tristan is shot in the leg, but the bullet was removed and he was bandaged up for now. Vadeed reveals he had found a piece of paper in the aforementioned briefcase. This paper (Image of Paper) includes information about an assault on a checkpoint, squads of soldiers called "Razors", and a project entitled X108.
UPDATE 6:(Suggested by Axonn)The group saw an artillery blast and felt it, only to find that the artillery blast left a car-sized crater not but 100 meters from the motel they are stationed in. Tristan whips out his map (Map Image) and begins to analyze it to try to find a more suitable place for the group to settle; far away form whomever wants them dead.
Spoiler: [b-The Backstory-[/b]]
2051. The UN disbanded twenty years prior, and the world is in a state of general disarray. Local governments are the superpowers of the world, and city-states have replaces all previous borders. The mass-chaos all sparked from one incident ten years in the past.

The former United States, seeking the reserved oil masses within the southern portion of the Gulf of Mexico bartered with the Mexican president to allow a small portion of Mexican soil to be purchased for the U.S. at a hefty price. 1.7 Billion dollars was the price tag, and President Richard Mollins accepted the deal. A harbor city was built on this patch of land, roughly thirty-miles in diameter directly on the eastern coast of Mexico. This served as a main dropoff point for oil barges. Ironically, the U.S. hadn't bought the Mexican-owned oil reserves within the gulf, and had began illegally drilling it's resources underwater; secretly. Once the Mexican government found out about this, they immediately overthrew the U.S. settlement. After many, many weeks of harsh negotiations, the Mexican Government cut off trade to the U.S., and used the remaining $856 Million to build a series of impenetrable roadblocks on key trade-roads between Mexico and the U.S., severing commerce. This double-edged sword forced Mexico to call upon Central American countries for financial support in exchange for a part of Mexico's ploy in the matters.

The United States tore down these roadblocks in an effort of "Stabilizing Homeland Security and Equalizing Prospective Trade". Mexico was enthralled, and declared war on the United States with the military assistance of all of Central and South America.

The U.S. was struggling to maintain a homeland foot-battle against the Central and South American soldiers, and the U.S. citizens were either in disarrayed chaos or in a bloodlusted frenzy at the frontlines. Thousands died in the initial invasion of the border, including multiple hundreds in two bombing attacks on Los Angeles, California and Austin, Texas. The United States urged its citizens, under the plea of Congress, to retreat into the Northern States and Canada. The Central/South American forces continued a general sweep through America, albeit heavy resistance of troops fighting in civilian-massed cities. The difficult combination of retaining constitutional rights to Life and protecting the innocent from warfare at the same time brought upon a situation with no chance of winning. The people themselves were simply too much of a factor to bring about a successful resistance. Mexico eventually claimed the southern half of the United States as it's own, and fighting ceased.

The recovery of the United States was nonexistent. The states simply disbanded into City-States after the war. Each has it's own laws, constitution, and policies; and each had it's own leader.

Spoiler: [b-The Story-[/b]]
The story follows Tristan Hollander's fight for survival amongst a makeshift squad of battle-met friends, who are taking on the roles of a sort of "homebrew soldier" in the last efforts to maintain peace between the borders of two city-states. They lie on the territory of the City-State of Ashburgh, while the border of the City-State of New Johnsville lies not but one half-kilometer away from their outpost. A run-down motel their base of operations, they survive this desolate snowy wasteland between two near-deserted cities, caught in the crossfire of their political feuds.

-Where You Come In-
After every post of the storyline, post a suggestion for the plot. It need not follow any specific character. It can be as vague or as specific as you'd like. Direct quotes can even be offered. You may suggest any modification to the story as you'd like, as long as it's relevant. Any characters actions may be suggested. If no suggestions are supplemented, the story will continue as I see fit. If the only suggestion/s is/are completely asinine, I'll continue the story as I see fit. Partial suggestions can be accepted if not all of a suggestion is relevant.

-What You Have To Work With-
Any time a map is referenced to, a picture will be supplemented. All documents that would require a readers knowledge of will also be supplemented. Any visual aids required will be supplemented. Sometimes, visuals will be supplemented for the sheer sake of being supplemented. Any of these can also be requested to be brought up in the storyline at any time.
Spoiler: [b-Characters-[/b]]

Tristan Hollander
Age: 27
Height: 5'9"
Ethnicity: European (English and German)
Traits: Short black hair, messy and unkempt. Brown eyes. Slight stubble. A scar on his lip from attempting to shave with glass; thusly, the stubble.
Attire: Black, faded vintage army jacket from some war in the past. "1971-Nam" is written in stitching in the inside coat-pocket. Under the jacket is a black shirt with a brown design on it. The design resembles a heart with a bullet from the top-V of the two heart crescents to the bottom point of the heart. He also wears blue jeans that aren't that faded, but do have a few dime-sized holes near the ankle cuffings. He wears black hiking boots.

Omasi Devvings
Age: 31
Height: 5'8"
Ethnicity: Australian
Traits: Dirty blond hair pulled into a pony-tail. Dozens of small scars about his body, one large one from his left wrist to his elbow. He has three piercings on his left ear.
Attire: Utilitarian slate-gray jacket with a small multi-pouch combat belt below it. A t-shirt is assumed to be under the jacket, as it is always up. Jeans or Cargo pants are seen on Omasi from day to day. He wears combat boots regardless of his other attire.

Craig Donnovan
Age: 29
Height: 5'6"
Ethnicity: East German
Traits: Buzzed, black hair. Goatee. A couple of scars on his upper body and one large one on his leg.
Attire: Ratty old blue jeans that are very worn in. One insulation shirt and one army jacket. Combat boots and a bandanna around his mouth.

Aryn Winters
Age: 27
Height: 5'7"
Ethnicity: English (South London)
Traits: Brown hair pulled back into a half-ponytail, leaving some of her bangs out. Her hair is naturally fine, and rarely requires washing to be soft or clean. She has porcelain-white skin, and she has green eyes.
Attire: Field Medic jacket with the medic patch torn off, blue jeans that are rather form-fitting, yet very worn in. She also wears hiking boots that have an insulation layer stitched into them.

Vadeed Shahrati
Age: 33
Height: 5'9"
Ethnicity: Iranian
Traits: Black hair that is messy and short. A light beard. He has one blue eye and one glass one.
Attire: Medic jacket with Kevlar patches in varied locations. Fitted cargo pants that are tucked into his combat boots. He also has a medic-bag sash across strung on a shoulder, crossing his chest.

Comments, critique, and story suggestions should all be posted here.

Cheers to Dave for influencing this RPG with his own creation, Safe. Amongst all influences of this RPG, that of which are innumerable, Dave's creation is by far the most unique and most polished of them all.[/i]

Cheers,
~Mosh
#364879 2 2007-09-14T07:18:27Z Mosh
UPDATE 1 - The First Post Has Been Updated With The Release Of This Update

Tristan walked over to a wooden table in the general lobby of the motel. His hiking boots sent an echo across the entire dusty room, reverberating off of every poorly-built piece of furniture near him. The ceiling lamp above the table flickered a few times, and eventually stabilized a flood of light. An occasional flicker here and there didn't bother Tristan, anyways.

Nearing the table, Tristan noticed a piece of paper folded twice, near the center of the table; just as he was told it would be there. He opened it up; It was from Omasi.



"Oh, that's lovely", proclaimed Tristan, as he crumpled up the letter and tossed it aside. "Who said they've got any right to control the food of one city, let alone two?"

He walked over to a window in the lobby, and stared outside at the blizzard for a moment. The snow wasn't letting up any time soon, and he knew this well. Over a foot had fallen in the past day, and ground-level doors were unable to open because of it. This made getting around the motel difficult for the seven remaining squad members.

"Craig, get your arse down here!" yelled Tristan. He had turned to face the door he entered, awaiting the entrance of Craig. "Hurry it up, will ya?!"

"Aye, mate?", Craig inquired as soon as he entered the room, faintly panting.

"Look at that note", Tristan said as he pointed to the crumpled letter on the ground. "Who in the four hells is 'Omasi', and why doesn't he want us taking food from wherever the hell we took food from?"

Craig walked over and picked up the note. He began to read it. "Omasi...?" he pondered while reading. "That's an odd name. Doesn't sound like it's from anywhere near here, mate. Maybe he's a cracked-out tourist?"

"A tourist who traveled here amidst global anarchy... right", remarked Tristan.

"Well, apparently he doesn't want us taking food anymore from his stock room. I can't remember ever having the squad get food from a stockroom, but we did raid a supermarket about three days ago in Ashburgh. We saw no one inside."

"Maybe he owns the place?" asked Tristan.

"Doubt it" replied Craig. "Ownership implies profit. Profit implies living people to interact with or sell to. As of now, we're short on that end of the stick in both cities."

"So what do you suggest? Take up arms? See who the hell he is? Eat like a king?", Tristan rambled on.

"Nope" snapped Craig. "I say we do nothing different. Assuming 'Omasi' is for real, he'll come to us. Let's just keep working on those repairs, yeah?"

[What shall Tristan and/or Craig do next?]
#365046 4 2007-09-14T23:24:36Z Mosh
Quote: Mechtradevil, September 13, 2007 11:24 pm
Explore each other's feelings, perhaps awkwardly and with sublety. If they are unfamiliar with each others background the characters can kind of flesh each other out some more. They should be repairing high-tech guns or a transportation unit of some sort.

UPDATE 2 - The First Post Has Been Updated With The Release Of This Episode

"Right..." sighed Craig. "The repairs. You'd think an electric generator would have an owners manual. But no. We had to steal the discount generator."

Tristan stared at Craig. His eyes burned a metaphorical hole through him, and Craig was lifeless to respond.

Finally, Tristan spoke. "Then throw it out or take it apart. We could use the scrap metal. Besides, how often do we really use that thing, anyhow?"

"...Good point" remarked Craig. "I'll inform the others."

"Good" replied Tristan. "Remember to ask Aryn where to put the scrap. She's always been peculiar with organization."

"Got it."

Craig exited the room, and Tristan stayed back. He faced the window once more and contemplated his thoughts. So much swirled around in a hellish hurricane of horrendous ideas that he simple tried to stop thinking. Hail chunks began to fall in extended intervals, and Tristan tried to count them as they plummeted to Earth. Anything to take his mind off of the day. It wasn't a good day at all. He had apparently woken up on the wrong side of the proverbial bed, it seems.

The jacket-clad tactician exited the room. He kept repeating to himself, "Must not show weakness. I'll bring them all down"; and this accomplished nothing more than the increasing madness of his psyche. He turned a corner to the left, and followed the path through the motel's hallways that he had assumed Craig has taken. Voices were off in the distance; serious voices, probably planning another raid plan to be presented to Tristan later on. The terms "flank" and "sweep" were heard numerous times, and Tristan was sure they weren't talking about flank steak or a chimney sweep.

"Tristan", Craig said as he poked his head out of a door leading to the hallway a couple of meters ahead of Tristan. "Aryn wants to talk to you. She says she can fix the generator, but there's a problem."

Tristan entered the room. "This problem involves risking life and limb, doesn't it?" he inquired. "Because if so, I'm only willing to lose three of you." The group chuckled.

"Nah" said Aryn, her brown hair flowing over her face as she looked up to speak. She moved it to the right of her face, behind her ear. It was naturally fine, and looked as if it had been washed hours earlier. "It's risky, but I know exactly what the part is, and where you can find it."

"So what's missing, exactly?" inquired Tristan.

"Oh, just a few mounting wires and brackets for an alternator."

"In English, please?"

Aryn sighed. "The metal things that hold a key component of our generator to the frame of the generator."

"Oh." said Tristan. "So why can't we just weld it on?"

"Because it's much more complicated than that. It's sensitive machinery. Put a torch in the wrong spot, and you've got a recipe for disaster."

"Story of my life" murmured Craig.

"What?" Aryn and Tristan both quietly inquired.

"Never mind. So, where can we find this bad boy?" Craig said, changing the subject quite quickly back to the topic at hand.

An eerie silence grew over the room as Aryn studied a large city-sized map in front of her. She rose her head up to speak again, and her hair once again fell in front of her face. She moved to the side once more. "There's a hardware store called 'Irons and Tires' that should have it. It has a well-advertised section on portable generators, including our model, from a few newspapers that were lying around. It should be there. I tried the CB on the local frequency, but to no avail."

"...Alright. How long will it take us to get there?" Tristan asked, a blank stare on his face.

"By foot, just over two hours." stated Aryn.

"Not bad. Who do you suggest for the trip?" Craig asked the general group before him, regardless of it's constitution of solely Tristan and Aryn.

"I volunteer myself" Tristan proclaimed. "I'd like to take you with me too, Craig. Maybe Vadeed too if we get injured. He's a medic after all. I think that should suffice and leave a bountiful pool of the squad here in case a weapon needs to be drawn."

"Good call" Aryn exclaimed. "Shall I pass on the word?"

"Nah. I'll track down Vadeed immediately, and we'll leave soon. I'd like to return before sundown - it's only two in the afternoon." Tristan said, a confident smile on his face.

"Lead on." Craig said, also smiling.

The two exited the room, and Aryn returned to her work. There was a closer destination to get the materials needed in New Johnsville, but the firefight that would surely follow wouldn't be worth it, she thought.

Tristan, Craig close behind, walked through the hallways searching for Vadeed. His sleeping quarters, room E5-17, was their destination. Upon nearing the door, a horridly rank smell filled the air. It was the last door in the hallway, only being met by a balcony perpendicular to the door. They both first inspected the balcony, and upon finding nothing as to what the smell was emitting from, they entered the room. A human lay face-down in a pool of crimson, no footprints or general distress about the room at all other than the corpse itself.

"The little bastard charged me, 'ey did." Vadeed exclaimed. "Callin' me a dirty halfbreed and all of that some-such."

"We're just glad you're alive. Who is 'ey, anyways?" inquired Tristan.

"Dunno. Said somethin' about working for the highest bidder. A simple slug to the chest is all that done 'em in." Vadeed said, smirking happily.

"Well, clean this up. We've got a raid of a hardware store, and you're coming along too." Craig proclaimed.

"Bah. Ruin my fun. I was goin' to torch him. But I'll throw him off the balcony if it pleases 'ya."

Vadeed dragged the corpse to the edge of the balcony and pushed it out of a hole in the railing, having been blown out by a haywire fragmentation grenade before the squad moved in. A fading trail of blood followed, and continued to trail until the edge of the balcony. The body bled once it impacted, releasing all clotting that had taken place earlier - if any.

"Done now?" asked Tristan, slightly annoyed by the body-shifting. One half-hour had already been lost to the event.

"Yes. You can lead. I 'avent half a clue in hell where we're off to."

"Alright. Let's go."

The group marched on. Lights in the hallway flickered often, only being illuminated by flimsy reserve power chargers below the complex, inaccessible to the squad. Litter, magazines, and old newspapers cluttered the halls, and made it difficult for the squad to move, but they eventually made it to a second-story fire escape. They traversed it down, into the fierce snowstorm outside, and began their journey.

What shall the squad do on their trip to Ashburgh?[/b]

#365115 7 2007-09-15T05:48:31Z Mosh
Quote: Axonn, September 14, 2007 05:18 pm
They run into some more people sent by the group that tried to kill Vadeed, and a relatively small fight ensues.

UPDATE 3 The First Post Has Been Updated With The Release Of This Episode

"Hey Craig" asked Tristan. "Do you have a map of our plan? Or did Aryn not give you one on your way out?"

"Oh, I've got one right here, mate." replied Craig, as he set his backpack down on a snowless patch of rocks and unfolded the map on the top of them.
Spoiler: Click to Show/Hide Craig's Map

"Pretty much," said Craig. "We follow straight until we hit a subway station, then make a 90-degree turn to the right until we hit another subway station. It takes cross-blocks to get to our destination, so a little improvised navigating is necessary, but we'll be fine if we stay close and move quickly."

Zing

"What the hell was that?" exclaimed Vadeed. "Was that a gunshot?!"

"Take cover behind the rocks. Craig, I want to know where that shot came from." ordered Tristan, who was assembling his rifle from pieces taken out of his backpack, behind the safe cover of a boulder.

"It came from the direction of our destination, mate. Three men. One's definately a gunner. One has a briefcase. The other is indistinguishable." Craig reported.

"Approximate distance?" asked Tristan, who had completed his rifle's assembly, and was now loading a magazine into it.

"Two hundred meters, closing." replied Craig.

"If they're from the same 'highest bidder' as the bloke who I met in my room, they're in for a treat." said Vadeed, who was loading one of his two pistols, preparing for a fight.

"Craig" said Tristan. "Take left-point. I'll fire suppressive shots."

"Yes sir."

Tristan lined up the general median of the group in his iron-sight. They were strafing left and right, causing a decent bead on them to be difficult. Nonetheless, Tristan fired a few rounds off. One of them actually struck the briefcase-carrying individual, sending him to a bloody slump within the snow. The other two were actively firing off "Hail Mary" shots at the squad, and only an inestimable number of them his the boulder, let alone the general proximity of the squad.

Craig shot off a round from his rifle, which had already been assembled upon leaving the motel. The single round stuck into chest of the main gunner of the approaching squad, and he kept on running. Bloodlust keeping him alive, it seemed. Three more shots Craig fired off, and they all missed. The opposing soldiers were now one hundred yards and closing. Tristan and Craig both began firing off aimed shots, hitting near them most of the time.

Finally, Craig shot off a round, and the bullet zinged into the stomach of the previously shot gunner. He fell forward into his own running momentum, and spiraled into a rather "broken" position within the snow. He had landed on his rifle's muzzle, and the impact squeezed his finger enough to fire off a round. That round flew through his shoulder, where the muzzle was positioned against, and into the sky. The last remaining soldier made a B-Line away, in retreat.

Vadeed popped up, hoping to not miss the last chance of a gunfight without shooting off a single round, and took aim. Steadily, he lined up a perfect shot between him and the retreating soldier, who wasn't running evasively at all.

Bang

Vadeed shot off a round, and the soldier dropped to a lifeless clump on the ground.

"Everyone alright?" Vadeed said, taking a general glimpse of his two allies.

"I'm good. You, Craig?" inquired Tristan, catching his breath.

"Nearly hit by a Hail Mary, but I'm fine." Craig replied.

"Shall we search them for anything useful?" Vadeed said, approaching the briefcase-carrying enemy's corpse.

"Search the bookman. Leave the rest untouched. We're fine on ammunition, and we don't need excess gear weighing us down." Tristan commanded.

Vadeed picked up the briefcase and opened it. Countless, meaningless papers filled the case - all of them with a large "X108 - POST DATED" stamp in the middle. A few papers were written in an indistinguishable language; possibly a code. "It's bollixed. I wish they'd make it easier 'an me and simply have a big arse stamp on the briefcase that says 'Warning: Contains useless documents'... Damn desk workers."

"Chill, mate. Keep it chill. There's nothing to gain by pissing on papers if you don't need to." Craig said.

"Who's pissing on what, now?" asked Vadeed.

"Never mind. It's just a saying." replied Craig. "Lets get back moving. We're only a few blocks away from our first checkpoint. I'm sure we can rest there for a few once we're there, too. Subway tunnels equal no snow, remember?"

"Good point. Let's keep moving, mates." Tristan said.

[What shall happen to the Squad, or what shall the Squad do next?]

NOTE: The first post now contains, and will now always contain, a "mini" version of what happens in each Update. This is so you don't need to search the entire thread for quick storyline info. It also lists who's suggestion was implemented.
#365232 9 2007-09-15T19:15:37Z Mosh
Quote: Axonn, September 15, 2007 04:57 am
They get to the hardware store, but they find it deserted and everythings gone.

UPDATE 4 - The First Post Has Been Updated With The Release Of This Episode

Empty, desolate city block after empty, desolate city block; the squad pushed forward. They were now in the city - deep in the city. The first checkpoint had been unknowingly turned into a roadblock by some random group of mercenaries, and they decided it was best not to put themselves at risk. Instead of continuing to the second checkpoint, a probable location for another roadblock, they continued straight north through the city. Using buildings and broken-down cars as cover, they weren't met with any resistance at all.

"I think that's it." said Tristan, point forward to a building with a large neon hammer at it's top, about two-hundred fifty meters away.

"I'd put money on it. Let's check this out." exclaimed Craig, smiling as he spoke.

It was below freezing outside - approximately -10C. They couldn't wait to get out of the snow, and into a building. Every now and again, a piece of hail would fall near them. A scary thought to know that nature can shoot at you, too.

They approached the doors. They were off of their automatic-opening slider bars, but that didn't bother the group any. A swift kick in the center by Vadeed sent them flying open, falling to their final resting spot on the linoleum.

The place was trashed. A few aisles only had garbage piled in it, but most of the building was destroyed. The outside showed no real damage from a person's point of view, so the destruction within was perplexing.

"What in the hell is that?" Tristan inquired, pointing to a large crater in the back of the store, illuminated by something above.

"I believe it's a crater." Craig said, sarcasm apparent even in his laugh.

"No shit. What's it fr- Holy mother of God." Tristan broke his sentence in two.

There was a huge, jagged opening in the ceiling above the crater. Tile was blown back around the blast-hole, and there was a noticeable increase in general chaos in that area. This worried the group.

"Holy shit. Was this hit by an air-strike or something?" asked Vadeed.

"No" replied Tristan. "If it was, the missile would have detonated on the outside. The crater's down here. Someone bombed this place from the inside."

"Well that's unnerving for the owner, but we just need our mounting brackets, and we're gone." said Craig, starting to look worried.

"Alright. Split in three, meet at the doors, behind the check-stands. Draw your weapons once up there and look for any outside movement." Tristan ordered. The group split up, as per request.

Vadeed took the left of the store. That section was mainly home appliances, so mounting brackets aren't completely excluded from possibility. Most of the merchandise was looted, and the display stands were all town down. With the exception of a few soaps from a broken display stand that Vadeed looted for the motel, which badly needed hygiene products, there was nothing of use over there.

Craig took the right of the store. Mainly composed of power-driven equipment and repair parts, this was an excellent spot to look for mounting brackets. Sadly, this section of the store was most heavily hit by the bomb, and was completely wiped out. All of the gasoline-incorporated vehicles and equipment were ignited by whatever flaming liquid had flown through the building, and they were all resorted to broken, charred piles of ash.

Tristan generally scoped out the center of the store. A few tie-down wires were lying around, possibly for a cardboard-box bailing machine. He put these in his backpack; in the largest open pocket. Wanding around some more, he found some clamps used for holding small components in refrigerators. While neither of these were what he was looking for, he continued on. Sadly, nothing else was in working order, or even in a condition to be looted. Trash, it seemed.

They all met up at the front in within the same minute, and all took out their weapons, as requested.

"I found some wires and some small clamps." said Tristan. "Nothing of true value, but we might make it work."

"Nothing useful found, but I got some soaps for back at the motel." Vadeed said; alert, and listening to his surroundings.

"I found nothing at all. The section that would most likely have the mounting brackets was torched." Craig said, smirking a little. "But this place did at one point have them, so Aryn's information was legit."

The group silenced for a little bit. They were looking around, outside, getting a clear and vibrant idea of their surroundings.

"Let's head home. We've done all we can." said Tristan, standing up from a prone position on the floor.

The group got up, assumed the three-point formation they traveled here in, and continued onward. The snow burning their faces as they were now walking into the frozen, harsh wind; this was going to be a long two-hour trip.

[What Shall The Squad Do Next / What Shall Happen To The Squad?][/i]

But, a note is left for them, from the highest bidder, explaining their situation (which is not good in some way) and one of them should be captured, or wounded by a hail mary from a rooftop.
UPDATE 5 - The First Post Has Been Updated With The Release Of This Episode

The group trudged on; bullet-battered barricades and snow-slaughtered scenery all around them.

Zing!

"Aagh!" screamed Tristan. "My leg!"

"Sniper!" exclaimed Craig. "Take cover where you can!"

Zing!

"Vadeed, get Tristan cleaned up!" yelled Craig. "I'll provide covering fire!"

Tristan did what he could to take cover behind a concrete barricade, with Vadeed's help. The bullet had lodged in his leg, although the bone was intact. The wound was bleeding profusely. Craig took cover on the opposite side of the street, using a broken-down family car as cover.

"You've got a bullet in ya' leg, mate." said Vadeed, wincing. "I'll need'ta pull it out."

"You'll need to pull the bullet out? It didn't make it through?!" exclaimed Tristan, grimacing in pain as another bullet narrowly missed them.

An unconcealed muzzle flash caught Craig's eye. "I see him. Within three-hundred yards; the motel with the blue sign at it's top."

"Can ye' make the shot?" inquired Vadeed.

"Not likely. I'll try if you'd like."

"For the fucking love of God, try!" screamed Tristan, as Vadeed slowly entered the wound with a pair of forceps from his medical bag. "Jesus Christ this is unbearable!"

Craig unleashed a few shots from his rifle, pelting the windows near the sniper's location, and having one shot go nowhere near his target. The shots from the sniper continued.

"It's a Hail Mary with this rifle, mates. Our best bet would be a detour, or waiting him out." Craig said.

"Agh!" screamed Tristan, as Vadeed began to remove the bullet from his leg; pouring alcohol in the wound the entire time.

"Awaiting orders, mates." Craig said, as he continued to fire off small bursts at the sniper.

"Lay suppressive fire and make your way over to us." Vadeed commanded. The wound was still gushing blood, but the bullet was out. Using one hand to slowly keep a steady flow of alcohol into the wound, Vadeed reached for some gauss and medical tape, and he began to wrap the wound.

Craig lifted the iron-sights of this rifle to his eye and took careful aim. With one pull of the trigger, he sent a bullet crashing through the top portion of the window where the sniper was located. The sniper's shots stopped.

"Clear!" Craig yelled, as he ran across the street to Vadeed and Tristan. "I don't know if I killed him, but I sure shut him u-"

Zing!

"-Negative. Keep low." Craig said, rather startled.

"Tristan, you won't be able to run that well at all, but you're as good as you'll get." Vadeed said, sweating a cold sweat.

"Alright. Make cover to the back that building" Tristan said, pointing to a building behind them. "Craig, we'll need you to lay more suppressive fire."

"Alright." Craig said, calmly.

Zing!

"Here's some more ammunition, too." Tristan said, handing Craig two clips. "Vadeed, you'll stick with me. Be alert."

"Yes sir." replied Vadeed.

The sniper's rather punctual shots slowed, but he was still visible in his window-slot some two hundred yards out. Taking this opportunity, assuming the sniper had run out of ammunition in his clip, the group made it's way safely to the back of the building. A few shots rang out, easily being heard bouncing off something that was made of metal - a car perhaps. Apparently, the sniper had reloaded.

"I found this in that 'useless' briefcase, mates." Vadeed calmly said. "I don't knows what'chit for, but it mentions a highest bidder."

"And why'd you wait until now of all times to tell us?" inquired Tristan.

"I didn't want to slow us down with tha' such of mindful preoccupations if we had run into combat. But seeing as we're being shot at now..." Vadeed said, almost suddenly nervous. "...I might as well show it to ya', in case I die a glorified death and such."

Vadeed took out a piece of paper from his jacket, and unfolded it.
Spoiler: Click to view the piece of paper

"Bullet holes?" asked Vadeed.

"I guess we shouldn't have been shooting the briefcase, itself." chuckled Craig. "Well at least we know to be on our guard."

"I guess. Quite unsettling that someone is hunting us, though." said Tristan, wincing at the pain of his wound.

They all read the note more closely, and realize that there could be a siege, and that there's probably a four man "Razor" squad lurking about somewhwere, giving more threats to think about.
UPDATE 6

"Razors?", Tristan thought out loud. "That can't be good."

"I know about the Razors." said Vadeed. "They're a mercenary group that is international between the U.S. and Canada. They're actually called the 'Razorstars', but 'Razors' just sounds easier on the mind."

"...Great." replied Tristan.

Just then, a rather pseudo-atomic shockwave shook the surrounding area. A simple forceful wave of heated air brushing against them, followed by some dust particles blown against their faces. In the horizon, a faint red glow was apparent, and a smoke trail rose into the sky.

"Someone ain't gonna be happy." said Craig.

"...You do realize they spoke of a siege on what is most probably our headquarters... right?" asked Tristan, very nervously.

"...Shit. Double-time to the smoke, guys. Base is that way, anyways." demanded Craig.

The squad ran, ran, and ran some more towards the smoke trail. Gunfire all around them, yet none of it directed at them - they were messengers in a turf war that no one wanted to kill. Literal explosions rocking the earth just feet behind them from slow-set land mines, Craig started to wonder if the route they took was the safest; albeit most direct.

Finally, they arose within sight of their base of operations. Not but one hundred meters left of the motel was a crater the size of a minivan, still blazing, with a thick smoke trail seeping out of it.

"...Siege, huh? More like fish in a barrel." said Craig.

"At least we're not Halibuts." said Vadeed. "Otherwise, we'd have to look straight at our impending doom.

"Search the place for any wounded. I'll keep a watch outside; behind that busted-down minivan near the entrance." ordered Tristan.

"Yes sir." said Craig and Vadeed, unanimously.

The group split up, and Tristan began spotting prospective locations on his map for the group to retreat to. This wasn't going to be an easy choice.

#372363 4 2007-10-16T04:42:20Z Mosh
Quote: LittleViking001, October 15, 2007 06:02 pm
Instead of copying and darkening, could you just create a new layer and paintbucket it with black?
It would have less precision, and the idea is to have a working copy to send to other pieces or areas on the fly. For all of my silhouette works, I save a copy of just the silhouette. Those things come in handy - I've used each of mine at least thrice in a multitude of endeavors.
I tried that method first, and it didn't work as well as one might think.

Also, one of the upsides is that the darken tool also shades the pixels one-pixel outside the selection box ever-so-slightly, creating an auto-fade effect so it's not as jagged as paintbucketing it.

Even moreso, just creating a new layer doesn't give you the vector-esque ability to create odd and disproportional lines and selection marks of transparency; which really looks great in the end.

#17623 1 2007-10-21T06:34:08Z Mosh
Both of the games were released one year apart, and by associated game developers NaughtyDog (Publishing Jak and Daxter), and Insomniac Games (publishing Ratchet and Clank).
They both feature a main character and a nonhuman sidekick traveling around planets and fighting off large, often egotistically devious bad guys, with slapstick humor along the way.
Both feature platforming and shooter gameplay styles.
Both feature various driven vehicles, upgradeable weapons, near-identical art styles, near-identical gunplay styles, and near-identical animations.
Both feature racing components.
Both have tons of sequels on different platforms.
Both have the sidekick "Saving The Day" at multiple points in the storylines.
NaughtyDog borrowed displacement mapping technology from Insomniac Games, in exchange for pixel-relation technology from NaughtyDog. Both games include these technologies, so both of the games include very nice, albeit very cloned versions of special effects.
Both include monetary systems that are earned by breaking the environments and/or killing enemies.
Both games include generic weapons, such as versions of a shotgun, versions of a machine gun, and melee attacks.
Both games have identical save/load systems.
Both games include at least one female character catching the eye of the male hero; which, in both games, causes the sidekick of the main hero to verbally antagonize or taunt the hero in multiple ways.

Now... which one of these games do you personally prefer?

I'd have to go with Ratchet and Clank - simply because I find it more fun to play.

~Mosh

#17819 1 2007-11-05T06:53:55Z Mosh
Well, since I'd dare not revive a threat - nor would I revive one full of obsolete facts regarding the game, here it is!
http://sco.gpotato.com/
Since the last thread regarding this game was posted, major updates have occurred. The game is no longer buggy, the client is bug-free (from what I've heard and experienced), and the graphics have been upped a bit - specifically the way particle effects look.

In a nutshell:
-Combat occurs within your ship - a customizable ship ala` Cowboy Bebop (fans of the show will immediately sense a reference to it; both in name and in gameplay/style). Your ship is your main attribute within the game, and it is the only thing that can determine your skills.
-Your pilot is simply an avatar for roleplaying purposes. It is also the means by which you move around stations which you land in - to buy things or sell things to/from shops, to make repairs to your ship, or to buy things from other players.
-The enemies range from ground-tanks, to enemy ships, to floating eggs of demonic space-creatures.
-Combat is fast-paced, and live-action. Fans of the game Freelancer will feel right at home.
-Skills come in a few distinct flavors: Buff, Attack, Heal, Defend. Buffs do just that - they buff you. Attack skills enhance damage output and sometimes directly effect weapons/the enemy. Heals heal... duh. And Defense skills reduce damage to you.
-You can craft your own items out of loot.
-You can repaint your ship, and even buy new ships (different ships for each of four classes).
-ALL classes have similar basic and advanced weapons. Within their skills is where they truly differ. The four classes are:
B-GEAR: Basic fighter. Can combat in the air and against ground targets with equal precision.
I-Gear: Sniper. Focuses on long-range homing missile attacks. They can also use skills to make it so enemies are unable to detect their attacks. They are mainly air fighters.
M-GEAR: Medic/Buffer. Their combat skills aren't amazing, but they can heal, defend, and buff.
A-GEAR: Shapeshifting ship. It can freely switch between aircraft and tank, allowing it to combat ground targets and air targets with easy. Very, very thick armor, but speed lacks. It has a long-range cannon.
-All weapons, armor pieces, ship components, and even ship color can be changed with new parts from the shop.

...Did I mention it's completely free?

Anyone else play this great game besides me? I'm still within my first dozen levels or so, so I'm nothing impressive, of course.

Mind you, this is quite a soft list of alternative rock. Bite me.

--The Postal Service: Such Great Heights
Awesome beat, nice lyrics. Soft and melodic, yet powerful and meaningful. Very nice song. Hell, even Kaiser Peremente (medical company) used it's intro on a commercial, and MTV uses it's intro quite a lot. Great mix of electronic beats and alternative rock.

--Snow Patrol: Chasing Cars
Strong beat and undertones, synthing of bells, and amazing lyrics. Powerful song.

--Radiohead: Karma Police
Lyrics that are soft yet capable of being yelled. Nice beat and great guitar work.

--Plain White T's: Hey There Delilah
I don't care what you think of this song. I love it. I can relate to the lyrics, and the acoustic guitar is great. Not to mention it's a good song to play if you're learning guitar.

And that's only to name a few.

Since drones depend on checking whether or not the tile in front of their path is alright for traveling into before they make one more "step", this wouldn't work. Invisible tile-like objects wouldn't work, because drones detect "solid" objects (tiles and closed/locked doors) to determine their pathing, and not any objects whatsoever. Drone paths aren't predefined, so the engine code upon which Drone's operate on would have to be rewritten.
It's possible, and it's a nice idea, but would require extensive coding to pull off.

For all who don't understand game development:
  • Games need someone to oversee the whole project. In small companies like this one, that would be either Mare or Raigan.
  • Games aren't just a program with a logo. They embody what the game development team ideals - the specifications that must come from dense teamwork environments, not just a logo in the corner.
  • Tons of games isn't any better than one awesome one. They've amassed this huge collective of fans that keeps on growing with only one game so far (albeit, an updating one). Quality OVER quantity, for sure.
Thusly, M&R don't need "more and more games" to expand. One awesome one every so often does the trick even better. A pile of crappy games won't play as well as one good one.
